title: Rolling Average
prompt: A chart smooths noisy values with a rolling average. Write a function that returns the average of every contiguous window of the given size. If the window is larger than the array, return an empty array.

explanation.beginner:
Example: rollingAverage([2,4,6,8], 2) produces [3,5,7]. Maintain the sum of the current window. When it moves, add the entering value and subtract the leaving value, then divide by the window width.

Compare “handles exact window size”: input [[1,2,3],3] produces [2]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Maintain the sum of the current window. When it moves, add the entering value and subtract the leaving value, then divide by the window width.

Tempting mistake: Recomputing every window from scratch repeats work; dividing by the full array length gives the wrong average.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated. A rolling-sum implementation takes O(n) time plus output space; slicing and reducing every window takes O(nk).

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles exact window size”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
